sourceConvention.experimentalReference: Belle and Belle II Collaborations, arXiv:2507.01249
sourceConvention.equation: Delta k_D contains K_W c_WW V_ti^* V_tj with K_W=[y_t^2/(16 pi^2)][-3 alpha F(x_t)/(2 pi s_w^2)]

nuisanceFirewall.publishedLimitScope: The Belle B->K(*)a(a->gamma gamma) result reports a one-coupling g_aW interpretation. It is evidence that the detector record exists, not a ready-made two-coordinate likelihood.
nuisanceFirewall.admissionRule: Promote the pair to an identified (A_2,c_WW) measurement only after the nuisance-profiled Fisher/Jacobian retains rank two with the full experimental covariance.

boundary.closed: The published finite weak matching supplies a mathematically independent row: its flavor-changing down-sector term is proportional to the unprimed direct c_WW, whereas the weak bosonic record sees c_WW-A_2/2. The two idealized rows have nonzero determinant.
boundary.notClosed: No existing published single-coupling limit performs the required joint fit, and the direct matching coefficient is loop suppressed. Existing B-decay data therefore nominate a realistic detector arm but do not yet resolve the sixth coordinate.
boundary.implication: The scale-sweep no-go has a concrete exit. Add a different process family—flavor-changing B or K decay—not another energy point of the same W-associated coefficient.
boundary.nextCalculation: Construct a joint likelihood using one W-associated high-energy kernel and B->K(*)a bins (visible and/or missing-energy), profile the listed current, CKM, form-factor, decay and detector nuisances, and test the smallest singular value against the preregistered resolution threshold.
